note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · ANNUAL MILLET, HEAVY HEAD
tiles.details: Introduced cultivated/escaped annual, often 30–150 cm tall, blades commonly 6–20 mm wide. Cultivar-dependent panicles may be about 6–40 cm, often heavy and variably lobed. Check fibrous annual roots and absence of perennial knotty rhizomes rather than calling species from head bulk alone. Existing photo shows head architecture, not a connected rooted voucher.
tiles.short: LOOK HERE FIRST: stout annual with broad leaves and a dense, often lobed or nodding crop-like foxtail head
tiles.status: WHOLE HEAD PHOTO — SAME-PLANT ROOTED HABIT NEEDED

tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE TRUE LIGULE
tiles.details: World Flora Online gives about 1–3 mm; Go Botany gives 1–2 mm. Separate the true ligule from hairs at the sheath mouth; no auricles. Existing physically archived Stefan.lefnaer collar photograph shows the source-labelled organ, but a millimeter-calibrated Texas specimen has not been verified.
tiles.short: Look inside the blade–sheath junction for a 1–3 mm fringed membrane or hair fringe
tiles.status: ACTUAL COLLAR PHOTO — MEASURED LOCAL LIGULE NEEDED

tiles.heading: 03 · BRISTLES ARE NOT AWNS
tiles.details: North Central Texas key generally describes 1–3 persistent bristles, while WFO/AusGrass regional treatments allow 2–5, up to about 15–16 mm. These are sterile reduced branches, not glume or lemma awns. Count several attached mature spikelets with a 1-mm ruler; no existing photograph independently resolves the exact bristle origin and count.
tiles.short: Count persistent basal bristles below a ripe spikelet; regional sources differ on 1–3 versus 2–5

tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE GLUMES ON A MATURE SPIKELET
tiles.details: Lower glume commonly 1–3-veined; upper glume 5–7(–9)-veined. Published upper-glume proportions differ between floras and cultivated forms. The physically archived source-annotated spikelet photograph teaches organ location but does not verify Texas measurements or author labels independently. No glume awns.
tiles.short: Spikelets about 2–3.5 mm; lower glume roughly 1/3–1/2, upper usually ~2/3 to nearly spikelet length
tiles.status: SOURCE-ANNOTATED SPIKELET — CALIBRATED GLUME MACRO NEEDED

tiles.heading: 05 · SEPARATE STERILE AND FERTILE LEMMAS
tiles.details: Spikelet typically has a lower sterile/staminate and upper fertile floret. Lower lemma often 5–7-veined, lower palea absent or small in regional descriptions. Upper fertile lemma indurated, shiny to finely rugulose; no long lemma awn. With mature material check the disarticulation ABOVE the glumes; do not infer the break point from an intact picture.
tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma near spikelet length; upper fertile lemma hardened, about 2–3 mm, smooth to finely wrinkled
tiles.status: REAL SOURCE ANATOMY — BREAK POINT NOT VERIFIED

tiles.heading: 06 · DON'T CONFUSE IT WITH NATIVE FOXTAILS
tiles.details: Three REAL different-species comparison panels already exist: panel 4 (zero-based 3) shows S. parviflora's reproductive bristles, panel 5 (index 4) shows S. reverchonii's slender interrupted head, and panel 6 (index 5) shows S. scheelei's longer projecting bristles. Panel 1 (index 0) is the introduced S. italica crop head. These images support visual comparisons but do NOT show connected perennial rhizomes or calibrated same-stage mature bristle insertion. S. parviflora has perennial knotty rhizomes and commonly 4–12 bristles; S. reverchonii has a slender interrupted head with sparse bristles; S. scheelei has long conspicuous usually solitary bristles. Annual S. viridis remains an UNPHOTOGRAPHED close look-alike; verify mature disarticulation and fertile lemma texture rather than identifying crop escape by head bulk.
tiles.short: Distinguish annual millet from knotroot, Reverchon's and southwestern bristlegrasses using roots and ripe bristle attachments
tiles.status: THREE REAL LOOK-ALIKE PANELS LINKED — ROOTED AND MATURE-SPIKELET COMPARISONS STILL NEEDED

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: FOXTAIL MILLET (INTRODUCED annual crop/escape): start with stout annual culms, broad foliage, and a heavy dense often lobed or nodding foxtail head. Flora of North America usually describes 1–3 persistent subtending bristles (to ~12 mm), NOT 'numerous bristles beneath every spikelet'. A crop-derived head varies greatly; distinguish from perennial native bristlegrasses using rooted duration, panicle shape and ripe spikelets.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: START with real SOURCE-LABELLED LIGULE photo 2: locate actual blade/sheath junction; distinguish the membranous or hair-fringed ligule from surrounding sheath mouth hairs. Source photo is unmeasured, so do not estimate length from pixels.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: World Flora Online gives about 1–3 mm; Go Botany gives 1–2 mm. Separate the true ligule from hairs at the sheath mouth; no auricles. Existing physically archived Stefan.lefnaer collar photograph shows the source-labelled organ, but a millimeter-calibrated Texas specimen has not been verified.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Lower glume commonly 1–3-veined; upper glume 5–7(–9)-veined. Published upper-glume proportions differ between floras and cultivated forms. The physically archived source-annotated spikelet photograph teaches organ location but does not verify Texas measurements or author labels independently. No glume awns.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Cultivated/escaped S. italica is annual and often has conspicuously thick, sometimes lobed heads; S. parviflora has short knotty rhizomes and usually 4–12 bristles per spikelet, S. reverchonii a slender often interrupted head and sparse bristles, and S. scheelei a longer, more open/tapered head with usually solitary long projecting bristles. S. viridis is another ANNUAL look-alike outside the installed set; head bulk alone doesn't establish crop identity.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

intro: FOXTAIL MILLET (INTRODUCED annual crop/escape): start with stout annual culms, broad foliage, and a heavy dense often lobed or nodding foxtail head. Flora of North America usually describes 1–3 persistent subtending bristles (to ~12 mm), NOT 'numerous bristles beneath every spikelet'. A crop-derived head varies greatly; distinguish from perennial native bristlegrasses using rooted duration, panicle shape and ripe spikelets.
memory_rule: MILLET=ANNUAL HEAVY HEAD (usually 1–3 bristles); PARVIFLORA=KNOTTY RHIZOME + MANY (4–12); REVERCHONII=INTERRUPTED SPARSE (2–8 mm where bristled); SCHEELEI=LONG SINGLE (10–35 mm).
safety_note: Three (not one) exact-species JPEGs verified physically in the canonical GitHub folder on 2026-10-23. Dedicated ligule and source-annotated spikelet photographs EXIST; the remaining gap is calibrated same-specimen bristle insertion, mature glumes and floret disarticulation, rooted annual status, plus controlled site QA. Do not claim detailed new arrows from these uncalibrated source photographs.
field_rule: Avoid native/introduced calls or true species ID solely from bristle silhouette. Count several attached mature spikelets and study rootstock on the same plant.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
